items.title: Senior Payroll Officer
items.description: Easygo is the Australian technology powerhouse behind global brands Stake , KICK , and Easygo Gaming . As we continue to grow our presence in Serbia, we’re strengthening our local People & Culture operations and looking for an experienced Senior Payroll Officer to join us in Belgrade. This is an opportunity to take ownership of payroll operations for our Serbian entities, Easygo Tech Europe and MB Care , supporting 200+ employees while working closely with our local People & Culture and Finance teams, as well as our global team in Melbourne. You’ll play an important role in bringing our payroll operations in-house — leading the transition from an external payroll provider to Pantheon, improving data accuracy, and helping us build more efficient and consistent payroll processes as the business continues to grow. The Role As Senior Payroll Officer, you’ll be a key member of our People & Culture team, responsible for ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant payroll processing across our Serbian entities. The role combines hands-on payroll management with HR administration, systems integration, and process improvement. You’ll work closely with local and global stakeholders, support employees with payroll-related queries, and contribute to the development of our internal payroll operations. Key Responsibilities Payroll Processing: Manage monthly payroll processing for 200+ employees across Easygo Tech and MB Care, ensuring accuracy, timely payments, and compliance with Serbian regulations and internal policies. Payroll Compliance: Maintain accurate payroll records and supporting documentation in line with Serbian payroll and accounting regulations, ensuring readiness for tax and labour inspections. Payroll Reporting: Assist with month-end reconciliations and prepare payroll-related reports and documentation, working closely with Finance. HR Administration: Manage payroll-related HR administration, including employee registrations, deregistrations and changes through CROSO, sick leave administration via eBolovanje/RFZO, and relevant processes through ePorezi. Employee Support: Act as a key point of contact for payroll-related queries, ensuring employees receive accurate information and timely support. Payroll Changes: Collaborate with People & Culture to ensure accurate and timely processing of new hires, terminations, salary adjustments, leave, overtime, and other payroll changes. Contractor Payments: Process contractor invoices, reconcile vendor accounts, resolve discrepancies, and manage queries related to contractor payments. Payroll Transformation: Support the transition from an external payroll provider to an in-house payroll function using Pantheon, working closely with implementation partners and internal teams. Systems Integration: Support and maintain the integration between HiBob and Pantheon, ensuring employee data, leave, overtime, and salary changes flow accurately between systems. Process Improvement: Identify and resolve data inconsistencies between HR and payroll systems, improve data accuracy, and help automate payroll processes across both Serbian entities. Who You Are Payroll Experience: At least 5 years of hands-on experience in Serbian payroll processing. Serbian Payroll Expert: Strong knowledge of Serbian payroll and accounting regulations, with experience ensuring accurate and compliant payroll processing. Systems Knowledge: Working knowledge of Pantheon or a strong willingness and ability to quickly learn the system. Excel Skills: Good knowledge of Excel, including pivot tables and lookup functions. Attention to Detail: Highly accurate and detail-oriented, with a strong focus on ensuring payroll and financial data is correct. Organised & Reliable: Excellent organisational and time management skills, with the ability to manage deadlines and multiple priorities. Clear Communicator: Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively across People & Culture, Finance, and external partners. English Proficiency: Excellent command of English, both written and spoken, with the ability to communicate confidently with international stakeholders. Bonus points if you also have: Payroll Transformation: Experience transitioning payroll from an external provider to an in-house or ERP-based payroll system. HR Systems: Experience with HiBob or a comparable HRIS, particularly integrating employee data, leave, overtime, and salary changes with payroll processing. Financial Reporting: Exposure to Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) concepts, including cost-centre allocations and departmental cost reporting. Accounting Knowledge: A basic understanding of general accounting principles. Why Join Easygo? Performance Reward: Annual bonus linked to individual and company performance. Professional Growth: Clear opportunities for development, learning, and career progression within a global organization. Health & Wellbeing: Private health insurance for you and your dependents. Office Perks: Daily catered lunch, snacks and beverages, parking reimbursement, and a modern Belgrade office. Global Exposure: Opportunities to collaborate with — and occasionally visit — our Melbourne headquarters . Team Culture: Regular team-building activities and a professional, collaborative working environment. We’re an office-first workplace because we believe the best collaboration, communication, and team connections happen when we work together in person. Our Belgrade office is our primary place of work, while we still offer flexibility to work from home when needed . Come as you are. Be part of something bigger. Click play on your career today.

items.title: Strategic Customer Success Manager
items.description: Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US. As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations. Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow. THE ROLE As a Strategic Customer Success Manager, you’ll own a book of enterprise accounts across the UK and Europe, acting as a trusted advisor who drives adoption, retention and growth. You’ll partner closely with Sales to deliver a seamless onboarding experience and educate clients on a completely new way to create video content. Engaging stakeholders from day-to-day users through to the C-suite, you’ll make sure customers see clear ROI and become true champions of Synthesia. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Reporting to the Director of Customer Success of the UK, you are energetic, driven, and care deeply about the success of our customers - As a Strategic Customer Success Manager, you will drive Synthesia’s future growth by building relationships with clients and turning them into happy users - You will be helping educate clients on a totally new way to create video content, and work very closely with sales to create a cohesive onboarding experience for new users - You are capable of engaging in business-level and technical conversations at multiple levels of the organisation, including the C-suite - Ideal for an individual who wants to expand their career with a fast-growing software company WE’D LOVE TO HEAR FROM YOU IF YOU HAVE - Customer-facing experience in Customer Success Management / Client Service / Account Management / Technical Account Management / Implementation or similar ideally in B2B SaaS - Experience in managing a Book of Business along with KPIs - A track record in managing risk, forecasting, and identifying growth opportunities - Establishing a trusted advisor relationship with our clients, driving value from Synthesia products and services - Successfully onboarding new clients and building key relationships in the first critical months and beyond - Coordinating and leading regular client check-ins with clear outcomes on client health and opportunities with senior stakeholder attendance - Light video editing using the Synthesia platform - Retention and growth of our enterprise clients - Ensuring ROI and value is understood by clients, proactively looking for risks and opportunities - You need to be fluent in English - Based in London. This is a hybrid role where you need to be in the office 3 days a week. WE’D BE PARTICULARLY EXCITED IF - Experience at a fast-growing technology company - Familiarity with AI or video tools COMPENSATION We offer a competitive salary, equity and benefits. Your offer will reflect your experience, skills and the scope of the role.

items.title: Critical Infrastructure Engineering Lead
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. Our mission Serve as Mistral AI’s senior technical authority for critical electrical, mechanical and life-safety infrastructure across assigned colocation sites. Protect the availability of high-density AI compute by identifying technical risks before they become incidents, challenging infrastructure operating practices and verifying that power and cooling systems perform within agreed requirements. Operating context & accountability Working with Engineering Operations leadership, IT Operations, hardware partners and colocation providers, you will provide hands-on technical assurance across a site or cluster. You will assess provider performance, advise on critical decisions, support incident response and ensure operational learning drives durable improvements. The role focuses on technical oversight and influence rather than direct management of the colocation provider’s maintenance workforce. Technical assurance and operational risk - Own and maintain the site technical risk register, including electrical and mechanical single points of failure, maintenance exposure, redundancy limitations, cooling capacity, liquid-cooling interfaces and common-mode failure scenarios. - Assess the resilience of utility connections, MV/LV distribution, transformers, generators, UPS, switchgear, busways, protection systems, pumps, cooling plant, controls and monitoring against the contracted operating envelope. - Review provider preventive maintenance strategies, schedules, critical asset condition and outstanding defects; identify maintenance deferrals and vulnerabilities that may affect AI compute availability. - Critically review high-risk methods of procedure, electrical switching and isolation plans, planned impairments, work sequencing, contingency measures, rollback plans and restoration criteria. - Validate the completeness and quality of technical documentation, including single-line diagrams, P&IDs, operating sequences, alarm matrices, capacity records, asset registers and operating procedures. - Use BMS/EPMS trends, alarms, power-quality records and cooling telemetry to identify abnormal operating conditions, capacity constraints and deteriorating resilience before service is affected. Incident response, investigations and reliability - Act as a senior engineering escalation point during major infrastructure incidents; rapidly assess failure domain, remaining redundancy, safety implications, likely IT impact and viable restoration options. - Coordinate technical information across the colocation provider, Mistral IT Operations and OEM partners, ensuring accurate incident timelines, risk communication and controlled return to service. - Review and challenge root-cause analyses, distinguishing immediate triggers from underlying design, maintenance, controls, process and organizational contributors. - Define and follow up corrective and preventive actions, requesting evidence of implementation and verifying that recurring failure modes have been addressed. - Identify systemic trends across sites and share lessons learned with engineering design, commissioning and regional operations teams. - Support emergency response planning and tabletop exercises covering loss of utility, cooling failures, liquid leaks, fire/life-safety events and critical equipment failures. Capacity delivery, commissioning and change control - Participate in design and constructability reviews for expansions, retrofits and new AI deployments; flag operational, maintainability and resilience concerns early. - Review commissioning and integrated systems testing plans, including power transfers, redundancy scenarios, controls failure modes, cooling recovery and operational readiness criteria. - Challenge test results and acceptance evidence against defined electrical, thermal and operational requirements; track unresolved technical issues through handover. - Partner with IT Operations on rack power and thermal limits, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, coolant distribution unit boundaries, leak response and load-restoration dependencies. - Assess proposed changes to critical infrastructure, including concurrent maintenance, controls updates and brownfield works; recommend safeguards and escalation where exposure is unacceptable. - Provide technical coaching to internal stakeholders, contribute to engineering standards and support recruitment and knowledge sharing as the portfolio expands. Success measures - Critical technical risks are identified early, prioritized and reduced through verified mitigation actions, supporting Mistral’s availability objectives. - High-risk maintenance and infrastructure changes receive timely, evidence-based technical review with clear mitigations and escalation. - Major incidents are diagnosed accurately, communicated effectively and followed by robust root-cause analysis and verified corrective actions. - New and expanded capacity meets agreed redundancy, electrical, cooling and operational acceptance requirements. - Repeat failures, unresolved high-severity defects and preventable technical deviations decrease over time. Minimum qualifications - 5–7+ years in critical facilities engineering, commissioning, data center operations or technical assurance in high-availability environments. - Strong practical knowledge of critical electrical infrastructure (UPS, generators, MV/LV distribution, switchgear and protection) and mechanical systems (cooling plant, pumps, controls and heat rejection). - Ability to review single-line diagrams, operating sequences, technical procedures, maintenance plans, commissioning evidence and root-cause analyses. - Demonstrated experience troubleshooting complex infrastructure incidents and influencing external technical teams without direct line authority. - Clear written and verbal English communication, sound judgment under pressure and willingness to travel and participate in incident escalation as needed. Preferred experience - Full technical governance, multi-site operations or mission-critical facilities serving high-density AI/HPC workloads. - Experience with direct-to-chip liquid cooling, CDUs, facility/technology cooling interfaces, water quality, leak detection and rack-level thermal management. - Integrated systems testing, EPMS/BMS trend analysis, protection coordination, failure-mode reviews and cross-site engineering standardization. - Experience partnering with hardware OEMs, design engineers, commissioning teams and infrastructure providers during live-site expansion. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. PRIVACY POLICY Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.description: Semrush is a brand visibility platform, empowering marketers to command their online presence and create measurable impact. We unify SEO authority and AI visibility, so brands are found, cited, and chosen everywhere search happens. That’s how Semrush gained the trust of over 28 million users—from scaling startups to Fortune 500 companies. Here, you own the way you work, but we move as one unbeatable team. We don’t just lead the market, we’re busy creating the world where Semrush is an unfair advantage for every marketer. We move fast in ways to help you grow. Here, you have room to experiment, keep what works, and learn quickly from what doesn’t. Ready to share our ambition and make an impact? Then, this role may be for you. About the role This product marketing leadership role shapes how we position, package, launch, activate, retain, and grow our self-serve customer base and is measured on that work's contribution to net-new and expansion ARR. You will own the positioning and launch narrative outright and co-own lifecycle KPIs with Product and Marketing. You will lead a distributed team of Product Marketing Managers and keep Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success aligned on shared priorities and metrics. Semrush is the platform marketers around the world already rely on for their SEO and AI visibility work, built over 18+ years. As part of Adobe, we are combining that product base with our proprietary data and Adobe's distribution and enterprise relationships to extend our reach. Self-serve is where so many of those customer relationships begin, and this role is central to how we grow them. Positioning. Persona- and JTBD-led, not feature-led. Every statement must be specific to Semrush and unable to describe a competitor. You champion a consistent standard for messaging quality (templates, worked examples, review tiers) and help the team apply it. Packaging. Lead the segment analysis, value research, and packaging hypotheses, and design tests with Product partners. Make clear, data-backed recommendations. Launch. Run a repeatable tier-1 launch framework built around a live narrative briefing for stakeholders before asset work begins. Translate releases into campaigns with new and expansion ARR goals and timelines. You are the center of gravity on messaging. Activate and retain. Partner with Product, Marketing, and Customer Success on the messaging, onboarding narrative, and experiments that turn new sign-ups into engaged users. Make sure what we promise in-market matches what customers experience, and feed retention and churn insight back into positioning. Customer insight and roadmap input. Run a standing research cadence (interviews, win/loss, competitive analysis) as protected work, and use it to provide structured market and customer input into roadmap planning. Be in the room early, and keep marketing and GTM colleagues across the portfolio aligned as scope evolves. Your team. Lead, coach, and hire PMMs across several locations. Build customer-focused, collaborative best practices and AI-assisted workflows that help the team do its best work at scale. About you Move together. Raise the bar. Learn fast—grow faster. That’s the default. And here’s what else is needed to succeed in this role: 8+ years in product marketing, including 3+ leading PMM teams at a PLG or hybrid PLG/sales-assist SaaS company. A record of setting positioning and running pricing and packaging work, and you can explain what you'd change and why. Fluency in funnel and lifecycle metrics and experimentation, and experience building KPIs with Data Science, Finance, and Analytics. A record of earning a seat in roadmap decisions by bringing customer and market insight to Product. Experience leading distributed teams. Strong executive communication. Hands-on with AI in your own workflow, and curious about how AI search is changing marketing. And the awards agree: Great Place to Work, DEI Workplace, Diversity Champion Award, International Inclusion Award, Most Women Friendly Employers, Best Place for Working Parents. All thanks to 1700+ employees who build the company every day. About our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion commitments Semrush is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, creed, color, national origin, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, ancestry, physical or mental disability, or medical condition including medical characteristics, genetic identity, marital status, military service, or any other classification protected by applicable local, state or federal laws. This job is not eligible for an apprenticeship contract. 📍 Betclic Group – 117 Quai de Bacalan, 33300 BORDEAUX

items.title: Design & Reliability Engineering Manager
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. Our mission Shape the engineering foundations of Mistral AI’s next generation of compute capacity while improving the resilience of the infrastructure already in service. This role combines technical design leadership with field reliability engineering: you will establish demanding, practical requirements for colocation power and cooling, scrutinize proposed solutions and turn operating experience into better designs, safer changes and more reliable AI capacity. Operating context & accountability Mistral deploys high-density AI infrastructure in colocation facilities, where partners operate the underlying critical plant. You will be Mistral’s technical counterpart to providers, designers, commissioning specialists and internal IT and capacity teams. The position combines forward-looking design authority with hands-on technical investigation and portfolio reliability improvement. It requires depth in one core engineering discipline and the judgment to lead multidisciplinary decisions with specialist support. Key responsibilities — design and technical standards - Own and continuously improve Mistral’s technical design criteria and colocation requirements for new facilities, expansions and retrofits, including availability objectives, failure domains, maintainability and operational flexibility. - Translate GPU platform roadmaps into measurable facility envelopes: IT load and transients, rack density, electrical topology, redundancy, cooling capacity, supply/return temperatures, flow, pressure, water quality and monitoring. - Review utility and MV/LV arrangements, transformers, generators, UPS, switchgear, busway, protection coordination, earthing, power quality and metering for suitability under demanding AI loads. - Review mechanical and controls architecture, including chilled-water and heat-rejection systems, pumps, control sequences, CDU integration, leak detection, filtration, water treatment and cooling recovery scenarios. - Lead multidisciplinary reviews of single-line diagrams, P&IDs, sequences of operation, design calculations, capacity models, failure-mode studies and proposed deviations; document risks and decisions. - Participate in site selection, technical due diligence, provider RFPs, design milestones and commercial technical schedules, challenging assumptions before they become delivery constraints. - Define design review and exception processes that balance performance, resilience, deployment speed, efficiency, capital cost and long-term operability. Key responsibilities — commissioning and delivery assurance - Partner with delivery and commissioning teams to define functional and integrated testing requirements, acceptance criteria, evidence packages and outstanding-defect management. - Validate that electrical and cooling infrastructure can support the contracted AI load envelope under normal, maintenance and credible fault conditions. - Review test scripts and results for loss of utility, UPS/generator transitions, cooling component failures, controls faults, CDU interface events and staged restoration where applicable. - Ensure operational handover includes accurate drawings, asset and interface registers, monitoring points, setpoints, maintenance constraints, emergency procedures and unresolved risk ownership. - Support live-site changes and capacity upgrades with a disciplined review of impact, sequencing, rollback plans and operational readiness. Key responsibilities — field reliability and root-cause analysis - Act as a technical escalation point for recurring or high-impact electrical, mechanical and controls incidents across operational colocation sites. - Analyze alarms, BMS/EPMS trends, event sequences, power-quality records, cooling telemetry, commissioning findings and maintenance evidence to distinguish symptoms from systemic causes. - Lead or challenge technical root-cause investigations with colocation partners, including common-mode failures, protection miscoordination, thermal instability, control logic, hydraulic performance and hidden capacity limitations. - Develop risk-ranked corrective actions and reliability improvement programs; validate effectiveness through evidence and post-change monitoring. - Identify fleet-wide patterns and feed lessons learned into reference designs, acceptance tests, technical specifications and provider governance. - Review maintenance and change proposals that create material exposure to compute availability, providing clear technical recommendations and escalation where required. Key responsibilities — collaboration and leadership - Work with IT hardware, network and platform teams to understand the operational consequences of rack-level and cluster-level failure domains. - Influence colocation providers, consultants and OEM partners through technically rigorous, fact-based reviews without relying on direct operational authority. - Present design trade-offs, reliability risks and investment recommendations in language accessible to engineering leadership and business stakeholders. - Develop reusable standards, technical playbooks and engineering knowledge sharing to support consistent decisions across a rapidly expanding portfolio. What success looks like - New capacity is accepted against well-defined electrical, thermal and resilience criteria with transparent technical exceptions. - Design risks are identified early, reducing late changes, stranded capacity and avoidable operational constraints. - Repeat incidents and unresolved critical engineering defects decrease as corrective actions are verified. - Field experience produces measurable improvements to future designs and live-site operating resilience. Minimum qualifications - At least 8 years in mission-critical data center design, engineering, commissioning or technical reliability, including responsibility for complex technical decisions. - Degree in electrical or mechanical engineering, or equivalent professional experience, with deep knowledge in one discipline and strong working knowledge of the other. - Demonstrated expertise in critical power and cooling architecture, redundancy, failure-mode analysis and operational risk management. - Experience reviewing engineering drawings, calculations, commissioning evidence and root-cause analyses, and coordinating technical specialists. - Ability to influence colocation providers and cross-functional stakeholders; excellent English communication and willingness to travel. Preferred qualifications - Experience with AI/HPC infrastructure, high-density accelerator platforms and direct-to-chip liquid cooling. - Knowledge of CDUs, facility-to-technology cooling interfaces, hydraulic performance, cooling-water quality and leak management. - Experience with electrical protection/selectivity, power quality, controls sequences, integrated systems testing and BMS/EPMS analytics. - Experience creating technical standards across multiple sites or providers, including design deviations and fleet-wide reliability improvements. - Professional engineering registration or equivalent technical credentials. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link. PRIVACY POLICY Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.title: Financial Data and Controls Lead, Billing Platform
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is seeking a Financial Data and Controls Lead to join our Billing Platform team. Billing Platform builds the systems customers use to transact with Anthropic: subscriptions, usage billing, quote to cash, invoicing, and payments. You'll be the dedicated owner of billing accuracy, reconciliation, and financial controls across those systems, making sure the right checks run, the right controls are in place, and the audit evidence exists. Our billing systems and pricing change often, and each flow needs to meet SOX requirements. Accurate billing is what lets us launch products and pricing quickly and still close the books on time. The hard problems today include validating negotiated pricing from contract to invoice, handling the many forms of credits, app store billing, and keeping controls current while the systems under them are replaced. This is a foundational role and the first hire of its kind on the team. You'll lead a working group of the reconciliation and controls owners from each billing engineering team, and you'll set the approach they follow. You'll work closely with Finance Systems, Accounting, Internal Audit, and Data Engineering. The role sits in Engineering and works with Finance every day. Our Data organization builds the pipelines and owns the warehouse, and you'll use that data and partner with that team. We're looking for an engineer or data practitioner with strong accounting domain knowledge, who can talk to engineers about systems and to Finance and auditors about risk and materiality. Key responsibilities Own reconciliation and accuracy checks for critical billing data (quantity, price, discounts, and invoices) across our product platform, third-party billing and payment providers, app stores, cloud marketplaces, and in-house systems Design and run detective controls that catch billing errors before they reach the accounting books Partner with billing engineering teams to turn repeat checks into automated verifiers Review billing changes that have financial impact, flag the ones that touch SOX or IT application controls (ITACs), and make sure functional test evidence is in place Make SOX review a standard, lightweight step in how billing changes ship, treated like a security review, so launches are not delayed by it Own the end-to-end test strategy and audit evidence for those changes, working with Finance Systems, Data Engineering, Accounting, and Internal Audit Triage billing errors, prioritize backfills and fixes with the owning teams, and track materiality over time Define and maintain the data contracts between billing and finance systems, so downstream teams can find and trust the data they need Lead the working group of reconciliation and controls owners across billing engineering teams, through influence and not reporting lines Act as the Billing owner, alongside Accounting and Finance Systems, for translating the product and pricing roadmap into financial impact, test strategy, and process updates Minimum qualifications Experience building or owning a financial ledger, billing reconciliation, or cash reconciliation system end to end, one that Accounting relied on to close the books Hands-on SQL skills strong enough to take two messy datasets (for example usage events and invoices), match them, find the breaks, and explain the root cause Accounting domain knowledge (order to cash, month-end close, and materiality) sufficient to tell which billing changes have financial impact Experience working with SOX and Internal Audit teams on IT application controls, detective controls, transaction monitoring, functional test evidence, and auditor walkthroughs Experience defining data contracts between billing or product systems and finance systems such as the ERP, general ledger, or revenue recognition Track record of driving work across Engineering, Finance, Accounting, and Audit without direct authority Ability to explain technical issues to Finance and auditors in their terms, and financial risk to engineers in theirs Interest in AI and a commitment to Anthropic's mission of building safe, beneficial AI systems Preferred qualifications Background as a backend, data, or analytics engineer who built a financial ledger or cash reconciliation system from scratch Experience running these systems under public company reporting requirements, and scaling them as the company grew Experience with usage-based or consumption billing Experience with multi-party billing, such as marketplaces, or app stores Experience turning manual checks into automated verifiers with engineering teams Experience remediating a control deficiency, or standing up a controls program while the underlying systems were changing A track record of using Claude or other AI tools to automate reconciliation, testing, or evidence collection, with checks that hold up to review Experience with billing and finance tools such as Stripe, Metronome, Zuora, NetSuite, or Workday Financials Python for data analysis or automation The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $345,000 — $425,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Fanatics has an established database of over 100 million global sports fans; a global partner network with approximately 900 sports properties, including major national and international professional sports leagues, players associations, teams, colleges, college conferences and retail partners, 2,500 athletes and celebrities, and 200 exclusive athletes; and over 2,000 retail locations, including its Lids retail stores. Our more than 22,000 employees are committed to relentlessly enhancing the fan experience and delighting sports fans globally. Overview Fanatics Betting & Gaming (FBG) is the online and retail sports betting subsidiary of Fanatics Holdings, Inc. As a Staff Engineer on the Payments team, you will be the technical owner of the systems that move money into, out of, and across Fanatics: deposits, withdrawals, and payments at checkout. The platform you will own serves Sportsbook and Casino today and is being extended to other Fanatics businesses. A key part of that work is letting a customer's shared balance appear as a payment option alongside cards and bank transfers wherever they shop, so that money already held at Fanatics does not have to leave and come back. You will also shape how Fanatics connects to processors, acquirers, and banking partners, with the aim of improving approval rates, lowering cost per transaction, and reducing the number of times the same funds are moved. This role combines deep backend expertise with architectural leadership. You will set the technical direction for payments across several teams and work closely with Fraud, Responsible Gaming, Finance, Legal, and Compliance partners to build payment flows that are reliable, cost-effective, and compliant with state regulations and card scheme rules. Responsibilities Own the architecture of the payments platform, including provider integrations, deposit and withdrawal flows, and the services other Fanatics businesses call to take payment. Design and build distributed services in Java and Spring Boot that process high transaction volume with strict requirements for correctness, security, and uptime. Build payment orchestration and routing across processors, acquirers, and payment methods, using approval rate, cost, and provider health to decide where each transaction goes, with failover when a provider degrades. Handle failure in third-party integrations by design, including timeouts, retries, idempotency, duplicate callbacks, partial failures, and reconciliation against provider and bank settlement files. Lead the technical work of onboarding new providers and banking partners, including evaluating options and defining the integration, testing, and rollout approach. Build in regulatory and card scheme requirements, such as per-jurisdiction rules and how transactions are classified, in partnership with Legal, Compliance, and Finance. Work with Fraud and Risk to bring risk signals into the payment path and to handle chargebacks and disputes, including how they are attributed when funds are used across businesses. Reduce payment cost through routing, provider terms, and design choices that avoid unnecessary movement of money. Set standards for security, data handling, and limiting PCI scope across payment services. Lead architectural reviews, design sessions, and incident postmortems, and mentor engineers across the team. Partner with product, frontend, and mobile teams so that payment experiences are consistent and clear for customers. Be open to occasional travel to Fanatics offices or industry events for planning, collaboration, and team development. items.title: CISO
items.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role Glean is seeking a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) to lead security for Glean as a company and for our core product. Reporting to the CTO, you will set the strategy and operating model across product and platform security, corporate security, detection and response, risk, and compliance, turning that strategy into measurable risk reduction. This is an executive role for a leader who combines technical judgment with strong organizational leadership. You will partner closely with Engineering, Product, Legal, IT, and company leadership to make sound security decisions at the pace of an AI company. You should be able to go deep on architecture and incidents, build a durable program, and communicate clearly about risk and trade-offs. You will Set a risk-based security strategy, priorities, policies, metrics, and decision-making mechanisms that scale with Glean’s business. Give executives a clear view of material risks, remediation progress, and decisions that require business ownership, with a clear operating cadence to ensure risks are visible, owned, prioritized, and reduced. Partner with Engineering and Product to build security into architecture, design, development, release, and operations. Guide security across application and platform layers, identity and authorization, customer-data flows, cloud environments, integrations, and AI-enabled capabilities, including models, agents, and the tools and data they can access. Lead a measurable vulnerability-management and secure-development program spanning threat modeling, code and dependency risk, software supply-chain security, penetration testing, bug bounty, remediation ownership, and validation. Use automation and AI-assisted analysis thoughtfully to increase coverage and shorten time to fix. Oversee security for corporate systems, identity, endpoints, SaaS applications, cloud infrastructure, and privileged access. Partner with IT and technical owners to improve preventive controls, monitoring, and operational resilience. Ensure the organization can detect, assess, contain, recover from, and learn from security incidents. Clarify escalation and decision paths; coordinate with Engineering, Legal, Privacy, Communications, and business leaders; and ensure corrective actions are completed and validated. Own security risk management, compliance strategy, audit readiness, and control effectiveness. Support frameworks and customer or regulatory requirements relevant to Glean’s business, which may include SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, PCI, and FedRAMP. Track meaningful outcomes in risk reduction, vulnerability remediation, incident readiness, and control effectiveness. Build and grow a high-performing team across security engineering, enterprise security, detection and response, and governance. Set clear ownership, develop technical and people leaders, and create an environment where teams can execute with focus and accountability. Build strong working relationships across the company, helping teams understand practical safeguards and make informed risk decisions without unnecessary friction. Partner with customer-facing security leaders on escalations and assurance needs. Contribute security expertise to commercial security products in partnership with their Product and business owners; those teams retain ownership of their product roadmaps. About you Senior security leadership experience with accountability for a broad, enterprise-scale security program at a high-growth technology or product company. Experience as a CISO, deputy CISO, or senior security executive is strongly preferred. Strong technical depth across product and application security, cloud and infrastructure security, identity and access management, secure development, and vulnerability management. You can engage credibly with senior engineers on architecture and remediation choices. Experience building and operating effective security, detection, and incident-response programs, including leading through high-severity incidents and ensuring lessons result in durable improvements. Practical expertise in security risk management, governance, compliance, and audit readiness, with the judgment to distinguish control completion from actual risk reduction. A track record of partnering with Product and Engineering to ship secure products and embed security in fast-moving development organizations. Experience building, leading, and retaining strong multidisciplinary teams; setting priorities; allocating resources; and creating clear accountability across teams. Excellent executive communication and judgment. You can explain technical issues and uncertainty plainly, recommend a path forward, and escalate material risk at the right time. You bring a collaborative, pragmatic leadership style that earns trust while holding a high bar for security outcomes. Especially valuable: Experience securing enterprise AI, machine-learning, LLM, or agentic systems, including data handling, model and application boundaries, tool access, and adversarial testing; using automation or AI-enabled techniques to improve security analysis, detection, investigation, or remediation; supporting regulated customers or programs such as FedRAMP; or preparing a company for public-company or IPO-level governance and disclosure expectations. Location This role is hybrid (4 days a week in our San Francisco Bay Area office). Compensation & Benefits The standard base salary range for this position is $424,300 - $489,400 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We’re committed to building and sustaining a diverse, inclusive workplace. We strive to attract and retain people with a wide range of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, and we do not discriminate on the basis of gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. #LI-HYBRID AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. As part of the interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about, design, and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required. Our full notice outlining how data will be processed as part of the application procedure for applicable locations is available in our Privacy Policy . By submitting your application, you are agreeing to our use and processing of your data as required. US applicants and their applications are subject to arbitration of disputes as outlined in our Applicant Arbitration Agreement . By clicking “Submit Application,” I confirm that I have read the Global Data Privacy Notice and the Applicant Arbitration Agreement , and I agree to the terms.

items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. At frontier scale, an RL run is a large distributed system: training, sampling, and environment execution run concurrently across a large fleet of accelerators and hosts. As an engineer in RL Engineering, you'll work on keeping that system secure as it scales. This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll work in the RL codebase and the infrastructure underneath it, alongside the engineers and researchers who build and use it. The system is large and changes as fast as the research does, so security work here has to keep up with that pace without costing performance or velocity. We're hiring from two backgrounds: security engineers who want to work on large-scale ML systems, and ML systems or research engineers who want to work on security. Strong candidates have depth in one and real interest in the other. Key responsibilities Design, build, and operate security controls for RL training systems and the infrastructure they run on Work across the stack (orchestration, environments, training, inference) wherever the work is needed Review designs and code across the RL stack, find security problems, and fix them Build shared libraries and tooling that other RL engineers and researchers build on Build the observability needed to understand what these systems are doing Work with researchers and performance engineers to make sure security changes preserve training correctness and performance Write clear design documents for what you build Minimum qualifications Strong software engineering skills in Python and at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or Go Experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems or security systems in production Strong understanding of security fundamentals Working knowledge of Linux, containers, and cloud infrastructure Experience debugging complex problems across many hosts and services Ability to reason about tradeoffs between security, performance, and reliability Strong written communication, including design documents Preferred qualifications Experience running ML training or inference infrastructure at scale Experience with infrastructure security, such as isolation, access control, networking, or identity Experience with container orchestration such as Kubernetes, and with sandboxed or virtualized code execution at scale Experience building observability for large fleets Experience supporting research teams or other fast-moving internal users Familiarity with reinforcement learning or large language model training workloads The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.title: Product Data Scientist - Youth, Families and Learning
items.description: About the role We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly. You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value. You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety. In this role, you will: - Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort. - Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit. - Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts. - Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments. - Turn findings into product decisions. Work with partners from initial hypotheses through launch and iteration. Recommend what to build, change, expand, or stop, explaining expected impact, uncertainty, and tradeoffs. Follow through to determine whether decisions delivered the intended results. - Build reliable measurement. Partner with engineering on instrumentation, dataset quality, and consistent audience definitions. Create reusable analyses and dashboards that make progress visible and let teams answer recurring questions independently. - Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete. You might thrive in this role if you have: - A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact. - Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design. - The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement. - Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority. - Comfort setting priorities independently across a broad scope, staying close to users, and moving between strategic questions and detailed analytical work. Helpful experience Experience with consumer product growth, youth or family products, learning and education, or generative AI would be valuable. We also welcome experience measuring learning outcomes, combining quantitative and qualitative research, or evaluating products whose value emerges over time. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. Join the Advanced Trading team within the Consumer & Business group as a Senior Software Engineer, Backend helping scale Coinbase Advanced trading products for customers around the globe. items.title: Compliance Program Manager — Regulatory Compliance
items.description: About the team Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) builds compliance programs and provides assurance for OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We combine technical understanding with practical operations to reduce risk, support product and research teams, and produce reliable evidence of how our controls work. About the role As a Regulatory Compliance Program Manager, you will build and operate programs that turn regulatory requirements into clear responsibilities, effective processes, and evidence that can withstand external scrutiny. Your work will focus on AI safety/security and content moderation, with privacy operations as an adjacent area. You will partner with Legal and the teams that build and operate our products to scope the work, maintain accurate control narratives, prepare regulatory responses, and lead external assessments for your assigned portfolio. You should be comfortable owning delivery, explaining tradeoffs, and changing your recommendation when the evidence changes. Success means controls have accountable owners, evidence stays current, and teams can respond accurately without repeatedly rebuilding the same work. The initial portfolio and expectations will be agreed with the hiring manager. In this role, you will: - Lead an agreed portfolio of AI safety/security and content-compliance work, including programs associated with the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, with Legal and relevant experts confirming applicable requirements. - Translate requirements into scoped programs, operating processes, control and evidence responsibilities, milestones, and clear escalation paths. - Build and maintain accurate control narratives and traceable evidence for regulatory requests, reporting, audits, and assessments. - Lead preparation and delivery for external compliance assessments, coordinate the responsible teams, and track gaps through verified resolution or an explicitly owned decision. - Prioritize the work that materially improves compliance outcomes and reduces risk; explain what should proceed, change, or wait and why. - Develop evidence-backed recommendations with Legal, Product, Security, Safety, Integrity, Privacy, and other functional teams. Obtain decisions from the authorized owners for legal interpretation, external representations, and risk acceptance. - Improve operational workflows for content and privacy compliance while keeping implementation and operation of controls with the appropriate functional owners. - Simplify and automate repeated administrative work, test the results, and verify that the improvement is adopted and produces accurate, reliable outputs. - Learn the GRC security-control environment and participate in the team’s on-call rotation, with scope and expectations explained during the hiring process. - Communicate clearly, surface uncertainty early, incorporate feedback, and develop the domain knowledge needed for the next priority. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have practical experience building and operating AI safety/security and content-moderation programs, and can explain your own decisions, contribution, and results. - Have used agentic tooling to automate and improve to scaled processes - Understand relevant technical concepts across model evaluation, training and release, safety controls, content moderation, and post-launch operations, and can explain where specialist input is needed. - Have a strong understanding of relevant AI safety, content, and privacy requirements, including the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, and experience translating them into operating processes and controls with domain experts and Legal. - Have led regulatory responses and external compliance audits, and can distinguish supported claims from evidence gaps. - Have delivered complex cross-functional programs, scoped practical first increments, and adapted priorities when constraints changed. - Have improved or automated an operational workflow and verified its accuracy, usefulness, and ongoing ownership. - Can maintain precise records, navigate technical/compliance documentation and contract language, follow through on commitments, and judge what to resolve directly or escalate. - Communicate clearly in writing and conversation with technical teams, Legal, leadership, and external stakeholders; explain evidence, uncertainty, recommendations, and tradeoffs. - Work constructively through disagreement, learn from feedback, and take responsibility for outcomes. Privacy program-management experience is a plus. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. items.title: Staff+ Software Engineer, Platform Safety
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Platform Safety builds the infrastructure that lets Anthropic bring its most capable models to more people, safely and securely. Our systems decide both who can access our most advanced models, and what capabilities they can access, wherever Claude is available. That includes identity and business verification, trusted access programs, and the core services that grant, hold and enforce model access across our products. These systems already power the Cyber Verification Program, which now includes Project Glasswing, and the Life Sciences Verification Program with further more advanced use cases in development. As a Staff+ engineer, you'll help set the technical direction for this work. The foundations are live and adoption is growing quickly, so the next challenge is scale: making access a matter of configuration instead of code, making verification reusable, and giving customers a consistent experience on every surface. You'll work closely with safeguards, product, design and research to turn safety policy into systems that are easy to use and enforce. You'll also take new 0 → 1 efforts from idea to delivery as new capabilities and programs emerge. What you'll do You'll design, build and operate the systems that decide who gets access to our most capable models. You'll build the platform that lets teams across Anthropic launch and run trusted access programs, moving access rules out of code and into data so that launching a new model or complex program is simple and scalable. You'll build out our identity and business verification system (KYC/KYB) as a reusable service that any program can use, which means integrating verification vendors, protecting sensitive personal data, expanding into new regions, and building fair review and appeal paths for customers. You'll also evolve the core services behind every access decision, including the services that grant and hold access and the customer and user identity models they rely on, and keep them highly available and consistent across our own products and cloud platforms. You'll shape the architecture through clear written proposals, review key designs, and mentor engineers on a growing team. You'll also share on-call, lead incident response, and support emerging new programs. You might be a good fit if you: Have a minimum of 8 years of practical experience as a backend or platform engineer, ideally at tech lead level or equivalent, and are comfortable working across the stack when the problem calls for it Have strong product sense, and work closely with cross-functional partners, including non-engineers, to shape and execute strategy in new domains Use AI tools as a regular part of how you design, build and review software Have designed and operated production distributed systems on a critical path, where correctness, latency and availability all matter Take full ownership of your work, from design through build, deployment, operations and iteration Navigate ambiguity and make sound technical decisions independently, have set technical direction that other engineers and teams adopted, and have ideally operated in both 0 → 1 and more mature settings Care about building robust, scalable systems that other engineers and businesses love to use Care about the societal impacts of your work and Anthropic's mission to build safe, beneficial AI Strong candidates may also have: Identity, access control or authorization systems at scale Fraud, risk, trust and safety, or KYC/KYB systems, including working with verification vendors Regulated or compliance-sensitive environments, including handling sensitive personal data Integrating with cloud platforms or partner ecosystems such as AWS, Google Cloud and Azure Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Location Preference: Preference will be given to candidates based in NY, SEA, SF or the Bay Area given the current location of team. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $405,000 — $485,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
